messages:
tay: brief follow-up to the streaming-retry thread: can we design a simple linearization contract so consumers never see non-monotonic output when we preempt+resume or hedge?

phil: curious: by linearization you mean a guarantee clients can stitch segments from different attempts into a single consistent stream?

tay: yes. idea: every emitted token attaches a monotonic watermark (logical offset) and each attempt publishes a stitch-id + watermark-range in trailers. client SDK uses watermark to dedupe/concatenate deterministically.

anya: that sounds promising. watermark avoids comparing raw tokens. but it assumes downstream runtimes can maintain stable offsets across restarts or resume. how do we get that cheaply?

rohan: runtime approach: checkpoints capture last-offset and a small resume-delta counter. resume handshake returns checkpoint-ref and next-offset. if resume occurs and offsets align, SDK treats subsequent tokens as contiguous. if not, SDK applies merge policy based on headers.

phil: merge policies? sketch options.

tay: propose three simple policies encoded in route config: "truncate" (discard overlapping new tokens), "prefer-latest" (use tokens from resumed attempt when overlap), "annotate" (emit boundary marker token like "[continued-from-ATTEMPT]" so clients can show manual stitching).

anya: code example for headers/trailers: ```
# request headers
x-rd-fence: <uuid>|<kid>|<hmac>
x-rd-resume-capable: 1

# accept headers
x-rd-attempt-id: 7
x-rd-stitch-id: ab12ef
x-rd-shed-score: 58

# preempt trailer
x-rd-preempt: reason=egress_slo;resume-window-ms=2500;checkpoint=kv:ckpt-7;range=0-512
# checkpoint ack from runtime (trailer)
x-rd-checkpoint: ref=kv:ckpt-7;hash=9f3b;range=0-512
```

rohan: important security note: stitch-id and fence must be tenant-scoped and HMACed. checkpoint refs should be opaque and ACLed.

phil: operational tradeoffs: watermarks require runtime to count tokens deterministically (byte vs token vs chunk). pick token-index for now; document deterministic tokenization rules in runtime contract.

tay: billing interplay: we can avoid double-charge when resume succeeds and checkpoint hash matches by marking earlier tokens as resumed and not billing re-emitted ones. if merge policy == prefer-latest, still only bill emitted tokens but mark duplicate range for analytics.

anya: hedging: if we spawn a parallel fallback, attempts will have overlapping ranges. stitch-id lineage helps SDK choose which attempt to display based on policy. we must expose lineage header: x-rd-branch-id so traces can join attempts.

rohan: small config sketch for route: ```
edge.stream_policy {
  admission: "soft" # soft preempt vs hard reject
  merge_policy: "truncate"
  resume_window_ms: 3000
  token_unit: "llm-token"
}
```

phil: observability: emit metrics per-stitch-id: preempt_count, resume_ok, resume_mismatch, merged_tokens, duplicate_tokens. add spans linking attempt ids.

tay: failure scenarios: if checkpoint persist fails runtime should reply NON_RESUMABLE; frontdoor then either hard-reject or auto-fallback depending on route. SDK should surface a non-resumable warning.

anya: tiny spike plan: frontdoor: emit preempt trailer with range; runtime stub: simulate deterministic token offsets and return checkpoint ack; SDK demo: stitch two segments using watermark ranges and merge policy. keep opt-in behind feature flag.

ci-bot: canary: rd/edge-linearize-spike created. owners: tay/frontdoor, rohan/runtime, anya/sdk. infra checklist pending.

tay: cool. we'll document deterministic tokenization and stitch semantics in RFC appendix. regroup next Thurs with demo clips. :metal:
